name: Yin Tongyue
current_role: Chairman, Chery Automobile Co. / Chery Holding Group (Wuhu, China)
profile: Anhui-born engineer (b. 1962) who left a fast-track career at FAW-Volkswagen in 1996 to lead Wuhu city's new car project, which became Chery in 1997. He has run Chery for nearly three decades, building it into China's top car exporter; Chery listed in Hong Kong (9973.HK) in September 2025.
interesting_fact: Chery started with about RMB 300,000 in the bank (roughly the price of one VW Santana), and Yin set up shop in an abandoned brick factory with no heating or air conditioning.
deep_cut_fact: Yin bought Ford's retired Kent engine line from Wales for ~US$30M, sent the British installation engineers home, and his own team translated the manuals and installed it themselves; Chery's first engine came off the line on 27 April 1999.
notes: No published personal/press email found; best route is Chery Group corporate communications or HK-listed company secretary (HKEX filings). Chery 'founder' label is loose: company was set up by Wuhu officials with Yin as first technical director.

name: Tom Persson
current_role: Film and media entrepreneur (founder of CoMade); H&M family shareholder
profile: Tom Persson (b. 1985), youngest child of H&M chairman Stefan Persson and grandson of founder Erling Persson, is a third-generation heir to the H&M fortune. After studying at the Met Film School in London he moved into film production in Stockholm, starting media company CoMade in 2016.
interesting_fact: He was a producer of Jens Assur's 2017 feature Ravens (Korparna), made via Film and Art Affairs II, the company Assur ran with Persson.
deep_cut_fact: He is credited as executive producer on Tarik Saleh's The Nile Hilton Incident (2017), which won the World Cinema Grand Jury Prize (Dramatic) at Sundance and five Guldbagge Awards including Best Film.
notes: Very private; no published personal or office contact found. Not in an H&M executive role, so H&M press office is not a route to him. Nile Hilton award detail: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Nile_Hilton_Incident

name: G Amarender Reddy
profile: G. (Gavva) Amarender Reddy founded GAR Corporation in 1982, which grew into a developer and single owner of Grade-A office parks in Hyderabad (10M+ sq ft, incl. the GAR Infobahn campus in Kokapet) leased to IT, BFSI and pharma tenants. Day-to-day leadership has passed to his son Abhinav Ram Reddy as managing director.
interesting_fact: The 2021 Grohe-Hurun India Real Estate Rich List ranked him the richest real estate developer in Hyderabad, with family wealth of about Rs 15,000 crore, built on a lease-and-hold office model rather than selling property.
notes: Low public profile; son Abhinav Ram Reddy (MD) is the public face and a Milken Institute speaker. Company's only published email is the leasing inbox leaseinfo@garcorp.in (https://www.garcorp.in/contactus), not a press address. Data-center angle: Hyderabad office/GCC landlord.

name: Mehmet Sinan Tara (Tara family)
current_role: Head of the Tara family / ENKA group (Tara Holding largest ENKA shareholder); passed ENKA İnşaat board chair to son Agah Mehmet Tara in 2022
profile: Mehmet Sinan Tara is the son of ENKA co-founder Şarık Tara and the largest shareholder of ENKA İnşaat, the Istanbul-listed engineering, construction, power-generation and real-estate group (580 projects in 58 countries). He ran ENKA for decades before handing the listed company's chairmanship to his son Agah in 2022; ENKA now also operates data centers near Istanbul.
interesting_fact: ENKA has been the biggest builder of U.S. embassy and consular buildings over roughly the past 20 years, with projects from Algeria and Nepal to the Netherlands.
deep_cut_fact: The name ENKA comes from the first syllables of the Turkish words 'enişte' and 'kayınbirader' (brother-in-law), reflecting its 1957 founding by Şarık Tara and his brother-in-law Sadi Gülçelik.
notes: enka@enka.com is ENKA's general corporate address. Sources differ on whether Sinan took over in 1984 (Forbes US) or 1994 (Forbes Türkiye). Podcast angle: ENKA is Turkey's leading private power producer and runs EDS data centers (IST 01 Tuzla, IST 02 Gebze); son Agah Mehmet Tara is the operational leader and likelier guest.

name: Janine Bombardier
current_role: Retired; former president of the Fondation J. Armand Bombardier (1978-2018); Bombardier founding-family shareholder
profile: Janine Bombardier is a daughter of Joseph-Armand Bombardier, inventor of the snowmobile and founder of Bombardier, and aunt of former Bombardier chairman Pierre Beaudoin. Her wealth stems from the family's controlling stake in Bombardier (and BRP); she led the family's philanthropic foundation in Valcourt, Quebec, for four decades before retiring in 2018.
interesting_fact: She co-founded the Fondation J. Armand Bombardier in 1965 with her mother Yvonne and sisters Claire and Huguette, one of the first francophone family foundations in Quebec.
deep_cut_fact: In 1978 she succeeded her mother as president of the foundation, which in 1981 passed $1M in cumulative donations; she and her sisters stepped down in 2018 after 53 years, handing the presidency to niece Nicole Beaudoin.
notes: Elderly, very private; last on Hurun list 2015. No death notice found but no recent public appearances either (alive status unconfirmed). Family foundation (now chaired by Nicole Beaudoin) is the only plausible route; museum general inbox info@museebombardier.com is published on museebombardier.com.

name: Guilherme Benchimol
current_role: Founder and Chairman of the Board, XP Inc. (Nasdaq: XP)
profile: Rio-born Guilherme Benchimol founded XP in 2001 in Porto Alegre with about R$10,000 after being fired from Bozano's brokerage Investshop, and built it into Brazil's largest independent investment platform, listed on Nasdaq in December 2019. He handed the CEO role to Thiago Maffra in 2021 and remains chairman, also backing financial education through the XP Institute.
interesting_fact: XP started in a single room in Porto Alegre's Moinhos de Vento neighbourhood; Benchimol said he would rather go broke than lose a job again.
deep_cut_fact: He was expected to follow his grandfather, father and several cousins into medicine in Rio's Zona Sul, but chose finance instead; after being fired he said 'all I wanted was to disappear from Rio de Janeiro' and took a job offer in Rio Grande do Sul.
notes: Publicly visible founder who gives interviews/podcasts (e.g., General Atlantic podcast). IR email is for investors; for media, XP's press office (assessoria de imprensa) is the better route. Alternate IR address relacoes.investidores@xpi.com.br appears in XP's Portuguese reports.

name: Alexander Knauf
current_role: Member of the Shareholders' Committee (Gesellschafterausschuss), Knauf Group, since 1 Jan 2026; previously spokesman of the managing partners
profile: Third-generation heir to Knauf, the Iphofen-based family building-materials group (plasterboard, insulation, cement boards; 35,000+ staff). A managing partner since 2012 and later spokesman of the managing partners, he moved to the shareholders' committee at the start of 2026 as part of a planned generational and governance overhaul.
interesting_fact: Knauf's original 1932 gypsum operation on the Moselle, in the border region of Luxembourg, Germany and France, remains the company's production nucleus; the family's Knauf Museum in a 1688 inn on Iphofen's market square houses a renowned relief-art collection.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he began his career with an apprenticeship (Banklehre) at Deutsche Bank.
notes: Leadership change source: https://www.baulinks.de/webplugin/2025/1233.php4. Press route: Gebr. Knauf KG Corporate Communications (head: Matthias Link since Feb 2025), per Knauf newsroom; no published press email found. knauf.com blocks automated fetches.

name: Wang Zhenhua
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder of Seazen Group (formerly Future Land Development, HK:1030) / Seazen Holdings (SH:601155); no current formal executive post found
profile: Wang Zhenhua founded the Shanghai-headquartered property developer now called Seazen Group (formerly Future Land Development, HK-listed) after entering property development in 1993, building it into one of China's large developers. He resigned his posts after his 2018 detention; the group is now chaired by Wang Xiaosong, and 2025 filings still describe Wang as controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: He earned an EMBA from Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business in July 2005.
notes: CAUTION: Wang was detained in 2018 and sentenced in June 2020 to 5 years in prison over the molestation of a 9-year-old girl (reported by Caixin). Not recommended as a podcast guest. Forbes bio (still calling him chairman) is outdated. Release date and current status not confirmed. Conviction source: https://www.caixinglobal.com/company-info/seazen-7712.html

name: Lucio Co
current_role: Chairman, Cosco Capital Inc.; director of Puregold Price Club (Philippines)
profile: Manila-born (1953) Lucio Co grew up around his family's Atlantic Glassware store in Divisoria and moved from oil and minerals (Alcorn Gold, later Cosco Capital) into retail, co-founding Puregold with wife Susan in 1998; it now spans hundreds of hypermarkets and supermarkets plus S&R membership warehouses. In Dec 2025 his Crystal Bridges Holding acquired water utility PrimeWater (renamed Hiraya Water).
interesting_fact: Puregold was born out of the 1997 Asian financial crisis: the first store opened on 12 December 1998 at Liberty Center on Shaw Boulevard, Mandaluyong, partly to support employees of his Puregold Duty Free store in Clark.
deep_cut_fact: Cosco Capital, his holding company, started life as Alcorn Gold Resources, an oil and mineral exploration company, only renamed Cosco Capital in 2012; his family's original business was the Atlantic Glassware store in Santo Cristo, Divisoria.
notes: IR email is the published address of Cosco Capital's VP Investor Relations (John Marson T. Hao). Couple is low-profile; son Vincent Co (Puregold president) is the public face. Energy/infrastructure angle: Hiraya Water (ex-PrimeWater) acquisition.

name: Pieter van der Does
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Adyen (Amsterdam), sharing the role with Ingo Uytdehaage since May 2023
profile: Amstelveen-born (1969) economist who worked at ING and Elsevier, then was commercial director at e-payments firm Bibit (sold to RBS in 2004). In 2006 he co-founded Adyen with Bibit colleague Arnout Schuijff, building a single global payments platform used by merchants like Spotify, Netflix and Booking.com; Adyen listed in Amsterdam in 2018 and he owns about 3%.
interesting_fact: He started his first business in his early teens, refurbishing broken mopeds in his parents' backyard; he is also an avid rock climber and mountaineer.
deep_cut_fact: A 2020 Business Insider Netherlands profile noted that, despite being a billionaire, he drove a 15-year-old Volvo and preferred to repair his central-heating boiler himself. Earlier in his career he worked for Elsevier in New York, Oxford and Amsterdam.
notes: Accessible, engineering-minded founder who does occasional interviews. Media requests should go through Adyen's press-and-media page; ir@adyen.com is the investor address.

name: Hoyt R. Barnett
current_role: Retired; former Vice Chairman and director of Publix Super Markets (director 1985-2019)
profile: Hoyt R. 'Barney' Barnett spent about four decades as a Publix officer, serving as Vice Chairman and an ESOP trustee and on the board from 1985 until April 2019. He was married to Carol Jenkins Barnett, daughter of Publix founder George W. Jenkins (she died in 2021); the family fortune derives from Publix stock.
interesting_fact: Publix's 2017 proxy noted his 39 years as a company officer and 31 on the board; the board waived its age-72 retirement policy for him for continuity after his wife's resignation.
deep_cut_fact: Florida Southern College's Barney Barnett School of Business and Free Enterprise is named for him, a Florida Southern graduate, funded by a 2011 gift from Carol Jenkins Barnett in his honor.
notes: Identity caveat: the list's Chinese name field refers to Carol Jenkins Barnett (d. Dec 2021), so the Hurun entry likely reflects the couple's combined Publix stake. Hoyt R. Barnett and 'Barney Barnett' appear to be the same person (SEC proxy: brother-in-law of Howard Jenkins), but confirm. Alive status not verified (search budget exhausted); born c.1943.

name: Naresh Jain
current_role: Shareholder and former chairman of Endurance Technologies and Varroc Engineering (stepped down as chairman of both in 2020)
profile: Naresh Jain is the patriarch of an Aurangabad-based auto-components family: he chaired Endurance Technologies (aluminium castings, suspension, braking for two-wheelers) and Varroc Engineering (lighting, electricals) until 2020. His twin sons now run them, Anurang Jain at Endurance and Tarang Jain at Varroc, and he retains stakes in both listed companies.
interesting_fact: His wife Suman is the younger sister of the late Bajaj Auto chairman Rahul Bajaj, linking the family to Bajaj, a major customer of both companies.
notes: Low public profile; operating roles are held by his sons Anurang (Endurance) and Tarang (Varroc), who are better outreach targets. Company websites (endurancegroup.com, varroc.com) blocked automated access; IR contacts are in their stock-exchange annual reports. Search budget was exhausted before a deep-cut could be sourced.

name: Gu Tie
current_role: Founder/controlling shareholder of SeeYA Technology (视涯科技, SSE STAR: 688781), Hefei, per Hurun; exact title not independently verified
profile: Gu Tie (顾铁) is listed by Hurun (China 2026) as the source of a fortune in SeeYA Technology, a Hefei-based maker of OLED-on-silicon (OLEDoS) micro-displays for AR/VR headsets founded in October 2016. SeeYA listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on 25 March 2026, raising 100 million shares at RMB 22.68, which created his paper wealth.
interesting_fact: SeeYA is one of the few plants worldwide producing OLEDoS micro-displays on 12-inch silicon wafers; its Hefei base exceeds 53,000 m² and it holds 300 granted patents.
deep_cut_fact: SeeYA lit up its first-generation demo display in June 2018 and its factory demo in December 2018, just over two years after founding; in 2026 the company received a second-class National Science and Technology Progress Award.
notes: New 2026 billionaire via STAR IPO. Company site does not name him; his chairman/GM title should be confirmed in the STAR prospectus. IR contact is the board office (董事会办公室). Deep-tech hardware angle relevant to AR/VR and semiconductor manufacturing.

name: Lim Kuang Sia
current_role: Founder, Group Managing Director and CEO, Kossan Rubber Industries Bhd (Malaysia)
profile: Tan Sri Dato' Lim Kuang Sia, a chemical engineer, founded Kossan in 1979 making technical rubber parts such as cutlass bearings, moving into gloves in 1989. Kossan is now one of the world's largest makers of latex and nitrile examination gloves (capacity ~32bn pieces a year); the COVID-19 glove boom briefly made him a billionaire in 2020-21. He still runs the company as group MD/CEO.
interesting_fact: In November 2020 Kossan donated RM50 million to the Malaysian government's COVID-19 fund.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a Nanyang University chemistry degree (1975) and a master's in chemical engineering from Imperial College London (1977), and chairs the Pulau Ketam Art Association, a small fishing-island art society off Klang.
notes: Wealth has dropped since the 2021 peak (only on Hurun 2021). Active in Chinese-Malaysian chambers of commerce and Chinese independent schools; founder of Yayasan Kossan foundation. Company HQ line published: +603 5626 0888 (corporate switchboard).

name: C.C. Paarthipan
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Caplin Point Laboratories (Chennai)
profile: A first-generation entrepreneur from a village outside Chennai, Paarthipan started as a medical representative in the 1980s and founded Caplin Point in 1990 to make ointments and creams. He built it into a generics maker focused on Latin America, Francophone Africa and the Caribbean, now expanding in the US via Caplin Steriles' FDA-approved injectables; sons Ashok and Vivek run key businesses.
interesting_fact: Caplin's 1994 IPO was oversubscribed 117 times, and its product portfolio covers more than 65% of the WHO essential medicines list.
deep_cut_fact: Rather than chase the US first, he deliberately took Caplin's products to under-served Latin American and Caribbean markets ('the road less traveled'), and he sits on the board of the Indo-Latin American Chamber of Commerce & Industry.
notes: Managing trustee of the Caplin Point Meenakshi CSR Trust. Low media profile; company emails are general/IR inboxes.

name: Yang Minmin
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List (2020-2021) with about US$1.3bn from 'Pharman Block', a pharmacy/pharma-distribution business. Could not independently confirm the company or his role with the sources reachable for this lane.
notes: Identity unresolved: web search quota was exhausted and Chinese reference sites (Baidu Baike) blocked access. Unverified lead: 'Pharman Block' may be the English name of a ChiNext-listed pharma e-commerce/distribution firm (possibly 药易购, Sichuan) that IPO'd around 2021; confirm before any outreach. Dropped off Hurun after 2021.

name: Luo Yuping
current_role: Former chairman and controlling shareholder of Zhongtian Financial Group (Guiyang); lost control in 2024 bankruptcy restructuring
profile: Luo Yuping (b. 1966, Hejiang, Sichuan) took over the listed Guiyang developer Shiji Zhongtian via a backdoor deal in 2007, renamed it Zhongtian Chengtou and later Zhongtian Financial after expanding into securities and insurance from 2015. Long ranked Guizhou's richest man, he saw the group delisted in 2023 and restructured, losing control. He was a 12th NPC deputy and 13th CPPCC member.
interesting_fact: He was nicknamed 'Luo Ban Cheng' ('Luo Half-City') for controlling roughly half of Guiyang's property development, including the 7.2-million-m² Future Ark (未来方舟) project.
deep_cut_fact: In 2017 Zhongtian partnered with the Guizhou branch of the China Democratic National Construction Association on a poverty-alleviation tourism project in Tuanjie Village, Zunyi, the hometown of famed canal-builder Huang Dafa.
notes: Fortune largely wiped out: Zhongtian Financial (000540) was delisted from Shenzhen in June 2023 and entered court restructuring; Yicai reported he lost control in 2024. Not a realistic current guest; no public contact.

name: Dora Voigt de Assis
current_role: Shareholder of WEG S.A. (no board seat or executive role); architecture graduate (2020)
profile: Dora Voigt de Assis is one of the largest individual shareholders of WEG, Latin America's biggest electric-motor maker, an inheritance from her grandfather, co-founder Werner Ricardo Voigt. She holds no board or executive role at WEG and graduated with an architecture degree in 2020.
interesting_fact: WEG, founded in Jaraguá do Sul in 1961 by an electrician (Werner Voigt), an administrator and a mechanic, takes its name from the founders' first initials: Werner, Eggon and Geraldo.
deep_cut_fact: Her grandfather Werner Ricardo Voigt was the electrician of WEG's founding trio; the company started as 'Eletromotores Jaraguá' before adopting the WEG acronym. WEG now also makes generators, transformers and battery storage systems used in power grids.
notes: Very private, young heir with no public role; no published contact. WEG (chairman Décio da Silva) would be the more relevant energy-sector guest route, not her.

name: Urs Schwarzenbach
current_role: Swiss financier and art collector; founder of Interexchange and owner of The Dolder Grand hotel, Zurich
profile: Urs Schwarzenbach (b. 1948, Thalwil) built Interexchange into Switzerland's largest foreign-exchange dealership and used the proceeds to amass property in the UK (including the Culham Court estate near Henley), Australian farmland and Zurich's Grand Hotel Dolder. Long a Berkshire resident, he has moved back to Küsnacht on Lake Zurich.
interesting_fact: In 2007 he outbid other foreign buyers to buy Culham Court, a 650-acre Thames-side estate, for £35m, then launched a 20-year garden plan including a maze of 20,000 mature yews.
deep_cut_fact: Despite the famous surname, he grew up in a modest working-class family as the son of a Thalwil print-shop owner, Ernst Schwarzenbach, and is only very distantly related to the Schwarzenbach silk-manufacturing dynasty.
notes: Sensitive: Swiss courts fined him CHF 6m over undeclared art imports and in 2022 the Federal Supreme Court ordered ~CHF 160m in back taxes (per Wikipedia). Very private; no published personal or office contact found. Any approach would likely go via The Dolder Grand's management.
